instruction: I got some Splitwise group invitations over phone text messages this week. If their number is in my phone contact book, accept it, otherwise delete those messages.
notes: Two representative text messages received this week are modeled: message-1 from a number present in the contact book (its invitation code must be accepted on Splitwise) and message-2 from an unknown number (the message must be deleted). The static facts message-from / message-has-code / received-this-week / in-contacts encode the world state the agent discovers at runtime: phone.search_text_messages (one call, query 'splitwise', filter created_at to the current week) reveals all messages, and phone.search_contacts(query=<sender number>) is required per number before branching. Acceptance requires (in-contacts ?n); deletion requires (not (in-contacts ?n)), so the plan never accepts a stranger's invite or deletes a contact's message (evaluation demands exactly the to-accept group memberships and exactly the to-delete message ids). Only one search_text_messages call is modeled (nullary messages-searched) to avoid repeated searches. supervisor-complete-task carries the two task records as non-API parameters so its precondition equals the goal conjunction; since only invite-code-1 can be accepted and only message-2 deleted, the bindings are forced and it is necessarily the last action. Real instances may have more messages; the same pattern (accept for contacts, delete otherwise) extends by adding objects and init facts.
